meanings.note: Casual, blunt contraction of あなた used between intimates or in heated speech.
Humble counterpart of もらう; volitional いただこう means 'let's take them / I'll have them'.

forms.title: Key forms of いただく

examples.text: お時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you spare me some time?

meanings.note: Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Prompts someone into action or shoos them along.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Attached to names of children, close friends, or familiar acquaintances.

examples.text: トシちゃん、また来たの？

meanings.note: Attaches to numbers/counters (二人とも, 三人とも) to mean 'both/all of them'.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Attaches to the masu-stem of a verb to form a firm but polite command.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Loanword from English 'glass'.
Muranishi's energetic younger partner in Sapporo.

examples.text: トシが外で待っています。
トシと一緒に来ました。

meanings.note: Counter/noun for a drink (especially alcohol) or a full cup.

examples.text: まあ、一杯やってくれよ。
examples.trans: Well, have a drink on me.

meanings.note: Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

meanings.en: cold (to the touch or in attitude)
meanings.note: I-adjective used for both physical temperature and cold-heartedness.

examples.text: そんな冷たいこと言うなよ。

examples.trans: I want to drink cold water.

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.en: be saved; be rescued; be a big help
meanings.note: Godan intransitive verb; 助かったよ means 'you saved me / that was a huge help'.

examples.text: 俺はトシだ。助かったよ。
手伝ってもらえて助かりました。

meanings.note: Na-adjective stem (also used adverbially).

examples.text: 時間は十分にあります。

meanings.en: bad; sorry (in past 悪かった)
meanings.note: Casual past 悪かったな admits fault ('that was bad of me / my bad').

examples.text: 今日は天気が悪いです。

meanings.note: Godan verb; 持ってくる means 'bring'.
Used with の to modify the following noun (次のお二人様, 次の駅).

examples.trans: I get off at the next station.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: I-adjective describing beauty.

examples.trans: Mama, you're looking beautiful today too.

meanings.en: cause; bring about; wake someone up
meanings.note: Godan transitive verb; 騒ぎを起こす means 'cause a commotion'.

examples.text: 次に騒ぎを起こしたら追い出すぞ。
examples.trans: If you cause a commotion next time, I'll throw you out.

examples.text: 朝七時に起こしてください。
examples.trans: Please wake me up at 7 a.m.

meanings.note: Godan transitive verb.
Compound godan verb from 追う (chase) + 出す (put out).

examples.text: 騒ぎを起こしたら追い出すからね。
examples.trans: If you cause a commotion, I'll throw you out.
Get kicked out of the house.

meanings.note: Noun form of 騒ぐ (make a fuss).

examples.trans: It turned into a big commotion.
